newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine use of installed capacity rises.
newsitem.headline: Argentine use of installed capacity rises.

text.p: The use of installed capacity in Argentine industry rose to 77.7 percent in August from 75.8 percent in July and 74.1 percent in August 1995, the private economic thinktank FIEL said Thursday.

"The use of installed capacity rose considerably in the sector of intermediate use goods, reaching 80.3 percent. However it fell in durable consumption goods, non-durable consumption goods and capital goods," FIEL said in a news release.
The statement also noted five percent of businessmen expect the prices of their products to ease within the next month, while the rest see no changes.
FIEL said eight percent of respondents considered the use of installed capacity in August as encouraging, eight percent as disappointing and 74 percent as normal.
